title: Why a prince stood barefoot in the snow | Folio 6 — The Honest Historian #Shorts
description:
Then Beyhaqi adds something he saw with his own eyes. On days of bitter cold and heavy snow, Masud would ride out to hunt. He would get down from his horse in the snow and stay out in the freezing air for hours, from one prayer time almost to the next. Sometimes, in that cold, he pulled on his boots with nothing on his feet. Why would a prince do this? Beyhaqi tells us Masud's own reason. A man must get used to hardship, he said, so that when a real crisis comes, he is not helpless. In Persian, the line is short and plain. Bar chenin chizha khuy bayad kard. One must get used to such things.
